summary: Martino Dibeltulo specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan (attested 2015) under doctoral supervisor Donald S. Lopez Jr. and mentor Ester Bianchi.

Marvin Eisenberg was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1939–1943) and Princeton University (~1946–1954). He held a post at the University of Michigan from circa 1949 to 1983.

Mary C. Wright was a historian and sinologist educated at Vassar College, Radcliffe College, and Harvard University. She curated the China collection at the Hoover Institution (~1946–1959) and held professorships at Stanford (1947) and Yale (1959, 1964).

Mary Evelyn Tucker works in religious studies, sinology, and Japanology. She earned her PhD from Columbia University (~1976–1985), served as Professor of Religion at Bucknell University (~1989–2006), and became a professor at Yale University circa 2006.

Mary Haas was a linguist who studied at Earlham College, the University of Chicago, and Yale University, working under Edward Sapir (~1930–1935). She held a post at the University of California, Berkeley from circa 1947 to 1977.
Mary Jaksch is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at the University of Sunderland under Peter Harvey (attested 2007) and also studied under Ross Bolleter.

Mary Shepherd Slusser was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Michigan, NYU, Columbia University (PhD), and Harvard. She worked as a State Department research analyst (1951–1958) and held curatorial posts at the Smithsonian.
Marybeth White works in religious and Buddhist studies. She completed an honors degree at York University and was a doctoral candidate at Wilfrid Laurier University (attested 2006).

Maryla Falk was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She held an academic post at the University of Warsaw from circa 1936 to 1939 and was a Fellow of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (1974).

Marylin M. Rhie was a scholar of art history, Buddhist studies, and sinology. Mentored by Harrie Vanderstappen and Pramod Chandra (~1965–1970), she served as a professor at Smith College from circa 1974 to 2013.

Masaaki Chikusa was a scholar of sinology, history, and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate from Kyoto University. He served as professor at Kyoto University (1981–1993; emeritus ~1993–2015) and at Otani University (~1993–2001).

Masaaki Hattori is an Indologist and philosopher educated at Kyoto University and the University of Calcutta under Shin'ichi Hisamatsu, Atsuuji Ashikaga, and Gadjin M. Nagao. He served as professor at Kyoto University (1961–1988; emeritus ~1988) and Osaka Gakuin University.

Masaaki Nitta is a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Fukui Prefectural College (attested 1983–1991) and Fukui Prefectural University (attested 1988).

Masaaki Noni is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Gadjin M. Nagao. He served as associate professor (attested 2003) and professor (attested 2013–2014) at Ryukoku University.
Masaaki Sugiyama was a historian of Central Asia and sinology who studied at Kyoto University (~1970–1978). He served on the faculty at Kyoto Women's University from circa 1981 to 1992.
Masaaki Tsuchiya is a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kokugakuin University (~1979–1988) and held a post at Senshu University beginning around 1993.

Masaharu Anesaki was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies educated at the University of Tokyo, Kiel University, and with scholars including Max Müller and Paul Deussen. He served as professor (from 1904) and library director at the University of Tokyo.

Masaharu Imai is a Japanese Buddhist historian who earned his doctorate from Tokyo University of Education (-1977). He taught at Ibaraki University and the University of Tsukuba (~1981–2005; emeritus 2006) and directed the Shinshu Cultural Center.

Masahide Mori is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history educated at Nagoya University and the University of London/SOAS under Tadeusz Skorupski. He served on the faculties of Nagoya University, Koyasan University, and Kanazawa University (associate professor ~1996; professor ~2008).
Masahiro Asada is a Buddhist studies scholar who was educated at Ryukoku University and served there as an associate professor (attested 1987).
